thread:
incident-bot: Pager triggered (P1) — routing anomalies: high 5xx rate + incorrect model variant reuse observed in eu-west-1. Auto-rollbacks attempted but some requests still returning v1 where v2 expected. Paging routing/oncall.
oncall-ida: I'm awake, taking ownership. seeing a big jump in route-prefetch misses turning into wrong-variant hits. isolating.
sre-jake: logs look like KV lookup returning entries with mismatched model suffixes. sample:
```
[2026-03-10T04:12:20Z] route-prefetch: lookup key=kv:eu-west-1:model:v2 -> returned id=abc123 (meta.model=v1)
[2026-03-10T04:12:20Z] serve: selected variant=v1 for request id=xyz789 (expected v2)
```
oncall-ida: that's the kv-prefix bleed I feared. appears the cache key generation changed after a policy rollout earlier (routing_policy.prefetch_v2=true) and older shards still have v1 entries. 😬
matt-eng-runtime: rolling back the policy change now. patching config: `routing_policy.prefetch_v2=false` via control-plane.
ops-bot: Received API call: PATCH /controlplane/config/routing -> status 202 (async)
oncall-ida: while rollback propagates we should stop smart-routing prefetched responses getting used. can we flip server-side check to enforce model-tag match on serve path? matt-eng-runtime?
matt-eng-runtime: adding a guard now — will reject cached entry if meta.model != requested_model. patch in flight:
```
POST /deploys
payload: {"service": "eng-runtime", "patch": "guard-cache-model-match"}
```
eva-product: tagging this as customer-impacting — some tenant queries returned stale embeddings + completions. product needs list of affected customers for comms.
cust-success-amy: I've started a shortlist from monitoring -> accounts with >1% error window: acct-42, acct-17, acct-88. drafting outbound.
oncall-ida: quick mitigation: evict the problematic KV prefix in eu-west-1 for model keys. plan:
1) pause smart-prefetch on router fleet (done via control-plane toggle) ✅
2) run targeted KV eviction for prefixes `kv:eu-west-1:model:` — starting

sre-jake: running eviction job now. command:
```
curl -XPOST "https://ops.internal/kv/evict?prefix=kv:eu-west-1:model:" -H "Auth: $TOKEN"
```
ops-bot: eviction job queued (job-id=evict-2060001). estimated ~3m to finish across shards.
oncall-ida: pushing canary traffic to fresh path (no-prefetch) to validate correctness.
matt-eng-runtime: guard deployed to 30% of runtime nodes, returning 412 when cached.meta.model mismatch -> logs show guard triggered and requests falling back to real-time model load.

sre-jake: eviction completed across primary shards at 04:18Z. confirming hit rate for cached key now 0 for the problematic prefix.
oncall-ida: metrics: error-rate back to baseline; wrong-variant responses down from 82% -> 2% within 6m after eviction/guard. good.
eva-product: can we capture a deterministic repro so we can add unit tests? also need a small public note for customers and an internal incident stub.
cust-success-amy: outbound email queued to affected accounts with explanation + ETA for postmortem. will include remediation steps we took.

matt-eng-runtime: follow-ups:
- add a model-tag to every cache entry and enforce on read (already half-rolled)
- tighten prefetch rollout gating (rate + shard-awareness)
- add automated KV schema migration steps to rollout docs
- add a canary check that validates per-region kv namespaces after rollout

oncall-ida: immediate mitigations done. handing to matt for follow-up. @matt-eng-runtime take it as action owner for post-incident tasks.
matt-eng-runtime: ack. I'll convene a retro and write runbook changes.

incident-bot: Incident record created: INC-2060001234. Severity=P1. Duration so far ~20m. Pager cleared from oncall after mitigations.
eva-product: please add a customer-impact section to the incident record and mark if SLA credits might apply.

cust-success-amy: adding note: 3 enterprise tenants saw degraded responses (partial data mismatch), no data loss, duration ~22m. starting scheduled customer calls for enterprise ones.

oncall-ida: quick notes to include in postmortem:
- root cause: routing prefetch rollout left mixed KV namespace entries; cache keys didn't include model variant tag consistently.
- immediate mitigation: rollback rollout, guard on read, targeted KV eviction, pause smart-prefetch.
- long term: schema-enforced keys, rollout gating, unit tests, canary healthchecks.

matt-eng-runtime: ETA for postmortem draft: EOD tomorrow. will attach logs, commands, and repro steps.

sre-jake: closing loop on ops: add an alert for "cache-model-mismatch-rate" so we catch earlier.

oncall-ida: thanks team. leaving note in channel: if anyone sees residual weirdness ping me. :heart:

ops-bot: Runbook task created: RB-4123 "kv-prefix-model-bleed" assigned to matt-eng-runtime.

incident-bot: Thread archived after resolution window.
